transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST - Duration 55m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dana (Acme CTO), Marcus (Head of MLOps), Samir (Infra)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Alex, AE on the account, and Priya is our SE. quick agenda: scope the benchmark, figure out harness integration and run plan.
[00:25] Dana (Acme): Yep thanks, morning — afternoon. We want a POC that proves latency and cost improvements for our summarization pipeline, and also validates private deployment options.
[00:40] Marcus (Acme): For context, current setup is a mixed CPU/GPU infra on EKS; we run a small beam search summarizer, typical request size ~512 tokens, 200 RPS at peak.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood): Great, that's helpful. couple clarifying q's: when you say 200 RPS is that concurrent in-flight tokens or per-second requests? also are you streaming responses to clients today?
[01:20] Marcus: It's requests per second. we do streaming for the UI but we also have back-end batch flows non-streaming for async jobs.
[01:38] Samir (Acme): And infra note, we have strict egress rules and SAML SSO. If we run any tests against your hosted endpoints we need to have a security review; otherwise we can run the harness inside our VPC.
[01:55] Alex: Totally understood. For the POC we typically support two flow options: Redwood-hosted harness where we run load from our infra (fast to iterate), or customer-run harness inside their VPC (preferred for sensitive data). we can do both.
[02:20] Dana: Success criteria for us are: p95 latency < 300ms for non-streaming baseline, streaming start-time < 100ms, and total cost per 1k tokens lower than current by 20%. also end-to-end reliability 99.9% for the window.
[02:45] Priya: Noted. we'll capture those as hard criteria. For benchmarking we'll separate streaming vs non-streaming tests since sampling and measurement differ — streaming needs client-side latency capture and server-send-start timings.
[03:10] Marcus: On workload sizing: typical payload is 512 tokens, but we have long cases up to 2k tokens for some reports. For the POC can we do 512 and one longer 2k test?
[03:28] Priya: Yes, we'll do a small matrix: 512 and 2k, and then step RPS from 50 -> 200 to verify scaling. We also want to test with and without prefix/KV cache to see amortized cost.
[03:48] Samir: That KV cache — do you mean KV cache in memory on the model server? we have concerns about memory blowup if long sequences and many sessions are cached.
[04:05] Priya: Right - Redwood runtime uses KV cache per connection, and we can tune TTL and shard size; we'll include that in the config. note: sometimes transcripts say "KV cash" in exports, lol, ignore typos.
[04:25] Alex: On the harness side, we have a python-based harness repo. it supports both streaming clients (websocket/http2) and non-streaming HTTP calls. We'll share the repo link.
[04:45] Dana: Do you have a dockerized runner? Our infra team prefers a container we can run inside our CI.
[04:56] Priya: Yes we provide a docker image and a sample compose for local VPC runs. we'll include sample prometheus metrics exporters too.
[05:15] Marcus: For measurements, we care about p50/p95/p99, tail latency especially for streaming start-time (time to first token), and also throughput cost curves. can you output cost projections per million tokens?
[05:33] Alex: We can provide cost estimates using our pricing model and also export token counts per run. We'll include a simple sheet that maps runtime metrics to projected monthly cost at different volumes.
[05:50] Samir: Security checklist: SOC 2 status, data at rest/encrypt, KMS integration, SAML/SSO, audit logs. we'll need that before any hosted-run.
[06:06] Priya: We'll share the security pack — SOC2 report, KMS notes, and details on audit log retention. If you want the private offer, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and air-gapped options.
[06:25] Dana: Good. One item: our legal will want to see data handling and deletion policies for cached content.
[06:33] Alex: We'll include that in the security docs.
[06:40] Marcus: Back to benchmarks — what's a realistic timeline?
[06:45] Priya: Typical flow: share harness + sample config (day 0), customer runs baseline (3–5 days to collect stable numbers), then we do a deep perf run with multiple seeds (1 week). overall 2–3 weeks end-to-end for baseline + detailed perf.
[07:05] Dana: That fits our quarter goals. We'd like a quick baseline this week though, can you expedite the repo?
[07:12] Alex: We'll aim to get the repo and instructions to you within 24–48 hours.
[07:20] Marcus: For the harness, we have custom pre- and post-processing in our script — it handles chunking and some prompt templating. can we plug our script into your harness or do we need to re-write?
[07:35] Priya: You can plumb your script into our runner; typical pattern is you provide an adapter that maps your input/output into the harness format. we can help with an adapter example.
[07:50] Samir: How do you handle streaming vs non-streaming metrics in the harness? we need per-connection start-time, total tokens produced, and any server-side queuing time.
[08:05] Priya: For streaming we instrument client to record time-to-first-token, and we capture server-side enqueued time when running in our infra; if running in-customer we rely on instrumented metrics exporters. we'll include sample Grafana dashboards.
[08:25] Alex: small note — streaming can mask some server latency if you measure perceived latency only, so we'll capture both first-token and end-to-end completion times.
[08:40] Marcus: About load: do you support sustained concurrency with connection reuse? our production uses long-lived connections to keep KV cache.
[08:52] Priya: Yes, harness supports both connection-per-request and long-lived connection modes. we'll include both runs in the matrix.
[09:05] Dana: Any concerns about model selection? we plan to test a 7B LLM and a 13B quantized variant.
[09:15] Priya: That's fine. kernel selection and quantization profile matter — we'll include recommended model/quantization flags and the runtime will pick optimized kernels. small transcription note: sometimes our docs say "kernels" as "kernelz" in quick notes — ignore.
[09:33] Samir: For the private deployment option, does Redwood require outbound connections to control plane? our security team is strict.
[09:42] Alex: Redwood Private can be air-gapped or with customer-controlled egress; control plane comms are optional depending on package. we'll mark that as a security follow-up.
[09:55] Marcus: Ok. Let's lock down the exact benchmark matrix so we can provision infra.
[10:00] Priya: Proposed matrix:
 - Model sizes: 7B, 13B-quant
 - Token lengths: 512, 2048
 - Connection modes: streaming (long-lived), non-streaming (request-per-conn)
 - RPS: 50, 100, 200
 - Cache: cold vs warm (with KV cache enabled)
[10:35] Dana: That looks good. For cost calc, we want per-request token count and total tokens.
[10:42] Alex: We'll include token accounting in the harness outputs.
[10:47] Marcus: One practical q: if we run the heavy perf test inside our VPC, how will Redwood access logs/metrics? do you want a push to your observability or will we share S3?
[11:00] Priya: We typically accept a secure S3 bucket or a Prometheus remote write. We'll provide guidance in the instructions for both.
[11:12] Samir: Perf noise is a concern. We need to ensure runs happen during low background load; we'll schedule dedicated nodes.
[11:22] Alex: Good call. We'll also run multiple repetitions and compute confidence intervals.
[11:30] Marcus: Anything else about streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs?
[11:34] Priya: Streaming improves perceived latency but can increase connection churn; non-streaming gives cleaner p95 numbers. For cost, batching behavior changes too. We'll measure both.
[11:50] Dana: On success criteria, re-iterate: p95 < 300ms non-streaming, first-token < 100ms streaming, 20% cost savings target.
[12:02] Alex: We'll treat those as target gates. If we miss any, we'll do optimization passes — quantization, batching, and routing tweaks.
[12:15] Marcus: Can Redwood run a small sanity run with your hosted infra first so we can compare numbers quickly?
[12:22] Alex: yes, we can run a quick hosted baseline and then you can run the private one. Hosted numbers will be indicative but not final for private configs.
[12:33] Samir: Please note our compliance approval is needed for hosted runs. until legal signs off we'll prefer customer-run.
[12:40] Alex: Understood. we'll mark that.
[12:45] Priya: I'll draft the step-by-step and include an adapter example for your script plus docker image tags.
[12:55] Dana: Great. On timeline: aim to get initial harness and instructions in 48h, acme to return baseline within 5 days, then follow-up deep run following week.
[13:12] Alex: We'll send calendar invites for the baseline check-in and the deep perf planning session.
[13:25] Marcus: Any docs or links you can share right away?
[13:28] Alex: I'll drop the harness repo link, security pack link, and a small runbook after the call.
[13:35] Dana: Thanks. End of call summary?
[13:40] Alex: Recap: share harness + docker + docs; Acme provides scripts + dataset subset; run baseline inside customer VPC or hosted as allowed; measure matrix (models, tokens, RPS, streaming modes); share results and iterate.
[13:58] Dana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

Summary auto-generated (may be rough): POC scoping call to define benchmark plan and harness integration. Decisions: use two token lengths, two model sizes, both streaming and non-streaming runs, RPS ramp to 200, customer to share scripts; Redwood to share harness and security docs. Next steps assigned.
